answer_text:
We need a map  
\[
f:S^{2n}\to \mathbb{C}P^n
\]
such that the induced map on top cohomology
\[
f^*:H^{2n}(\mathbb{C}P^n;\mathbb{Z})\to H^{2n}(S^{2n};\mathbb{Z})
\]
is an isomorphism.

Recall the integral cohomology ring of complex projective space:
\[
H^*(\mathbb{C}P^n;\mathbb{Z})\cong \mathbb{Z}[x]/(x^{n+1}),
\]
where \(\deg x=2\). In particular,
\[
H^{2n}(\mathbb{C}P^n;\mathbb{Z})\cong \mathbb{Z}
\]
and is generated by \(x^n\).

Also,
\[
H^{2n}(S^{2n};\mathbb{Z})\cong \mathbb{Z}.
\]

Now consider \(f^*\). Since cohomology is a contravariant ring homomorphism, we have
\[
f^*(x^n)=(f^*(x))^n.
\]

For \(n>1\), we have \(2n\ge 4\), so
\[
H^2(S^{2n};\mathbb{Z})=0.
\]
Thus
\[
f^*(x)=0\in H^2(S^{2n};\mathbb{Z}).
\]
Therefore,
\[
f^*(x^n)=(f^*(x))^n=0.
\]
But \(f^*(x^n)\) must then be the image of the generator of \(H^{2n}(\mathbb{C}P^n;\mathbb{Z})\), so \(f^*\) on \(H^{2n}\) would be the zero map, not an isomorphism. Hence no such map exists for \(n>1\).

For \(n=1\), we have
\[
S^2\to \mathbb{C}P^1\cong S^2.
\]
A degree \(1\) homeomorphism works, and it induces an isomorphism
\[
H^2(\mathbb{C}P^1;\mathbb{Z})\cong \mathbb{Z}\to H^2(S^2;\mathbb{Z})\cong \mathbb{Z}.
\]

Therefore the only natural number \(n\) with the required property is

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
